planner_plan.rationale: The delay has two identified contributors: tenant PRB contention (radio side) and queue build-up on bearers (transport side). This is the only workflow covering both: KPM measures MAC/PRB pressure and delay KPIs, SLICE enforces tenant PRB policy to relieve contention, TC addresses bearer queue build-up, and RC validates the end-to-end result. slice-assurance omits the TC/queue dimension and transport-qos omits PRB contention, so each would leave half the problem unaddressed.

planner_plan.rationale: ECN marking on the default bearer queue is transport active queue management, so TC is the actuating agent and apply-codel is its AQM profile action. TC consumes DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, which only KPM produces, so KPM runs first with observe-ue (UE/DRB-oriented records) to satisfy the data dependency and baseline queueing delay. RC is excluded: ECN is a transport-level queue policy, not a per-UE E2SM-RC radio bearer control, and on this emulator an RC CONTROL-ACK would add no effect. Slice is excluded since no PRB partitioning is involved. No operator template is invoked by name, so a novel 2-step chain is composed, consistent with the operator's accepted minimal transport chains. Risks: TC control on the emulator may not shift downstream KPIs, so validate via TC's RLC.queue_stats output; if delay evidence is needed post-change, follow with a KPM observe-ue check. Next best action: execute kpm observe-ue, then tc apply-codel to enable ECN marking.
